findings.description: The bucket has no ACL restriction (defaults to public in this context per the comment) and is explicitly noted as public, allowing unauthenticated users to read/write objects including sensitive files.

No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket (including customer master data) are not encrypted at rest, risking data exposure if underlying storage is compromised.
A customer master spreadsheet is uploaded to a publicly accessible, unencrypted S3 bucket, exposing sensitive customer data to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is set, leaving financial data unencrypted at rest and vulnerable to exposure if storage-level access controls fail.
No server-side encryption is configured for this bucket, leaving operational data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is present, so data science bucket contents are stored unencrypted, risking exposure of potentially sensitive datasets.
